title: Maximum Spending After Buying Items
summary: Given an m * n matrix of item values, where each shop's items are sorted in non-increasing order, you are to buy one item per day from any shop.
statement: Given an m * n matrix of item values, where each shop's items are sorted in non-increasing order, you are to buy one item per day from any shop. The cost of buying an item on the d^th day is its value multiplied by d. The items are distinct across all shops. The goal is to determine the maximum total cost of buying all items.
constraints: Each shop row is nonincreasing; only its rightmost remaining item may be bought.
Exactly one item is bought per day and costs day times value; maximize total spending.
hints: Larger values should receive later, larger day multipliers whenever access constraints allow.
Put each row’s accessible rightmost item in a min-heap and reveal its left neighbor after purchase.
Pop the smallest available value each day and multiply by the day number.
An exchange argument moves any smaller accessible purchase earlier without decreasing later opportunities or total spending.
editorial: An exchange argument moves any smaller accessible purchase earlier without decreasing later opportunities or total spending.

tests.explanation: Buying currently cheapest available items first reserves large values for later multipliers, totaling 285.
A min-heap merges the accessible row suffixes in globally increasing order.
